# Proof@home

> Proof@home is a community program, like Folding@home but for proving software correct. Volunteers point their own coding agents, such as Claude Code or Codex, at small formal-verification tasks in open-source infrastructure. Every proof is checked again with a pinned verifier such as Verus or Kani, and only proofs that hold go to the project.

Proof@home is at an early stage and not yet open to contributors. The problem file format is published. The command-line tool and MCP server that contributors will use are being built.

How it works:

- Maintainers decide what should be proved about their code. Contributors never change what is proved, only how.
- A contributor's agent runs on their own computer. Proof@home never sees their login or their model traffic.
- Every result is re-checked automatically before a person reviews it.
- Accepted proofs go to the project in small, reviewed batches, credited to the contributor.
- The first focus is Rust code that runs virtual machines.

## Docs

- [Website](https://proofathome.org/): the goal and the vision
- [Source code](https://github.com/proofathome/proofathome): the Proof@home repository on GitHub
- [Problem file format](https://github.com/proofathome/proofathome/blob/main/docs/problem-format.md): how a proof task is described
- [Rust crate](https://crates.io/crates/proofathome): the published parser for problem files
